decisive_items: right-sided chest pain that worsened with inspiration
severe sweating confined to his right arm and thoracic area
decreased surface temperature over the right arm and right thorax corresponding to dermatomes C5–T12
response.rationale: Pancoast tumor best explains the apical lung infiltrate with ipsilateral autonomic symptoms (sweating, coolness) and pleuritic pain; absence of smoking is not exclusionary. Horner's syndrome is contradicted by normal pupils and eyelids. CRPS lacks a precipitating injury and does not explain the pulmonary infiltrate.

rejected.why: Pupils equal and reactive, no ptosis; Horner's syndrome explicitly contradicted.
No trauma or inciting event; pulmonary infiltrate and pleural rub unexplained by CRPS.
